guards.what: LIQUIFY_GROUND's six Frantic Escapes are added at a RANDOM pile position; the sim appends the discard half
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-28: all SIX Frantic Escapes now take a Shuffle-stream draw and land at a random slot. TheInsatiable._add_escape_to_discard (the_insatiable.py:71-93) inlines the same primitive add_to_draw uses -- `discard_pile.insert(crng.shuffle.randrange(count+1), card)` in parity, the shared rng in legacy -- instead of calling the appending CardPileCmd.add_to_discard, matching TheInsatiable.cs:130-137 (one loop over i in [0,6) where only the PileType changes at i==3, every add passing CardPilePosition.Random) and CardPileCmd.cs:510-514, which resolves Random to `Rng.Shuffle.NextInt(targetPile.Cards.Count + 1)` for BOTH pile types. The discard's orientation needs no index flip (index 0 = top on both sides), which the code documents. WAS: 3 Shuffle draws instead of 6, and the three discard-pile Escapes appended at the bottom in a fixed order. The rule-3 conflict this entry reported against audit/records/power/sandpit.json's 'Frantic Escape as the counterplay' guard is now moot.

guards.issue: TheInsatiable.cs:96 telegraphs `new BuffIntent(), new StatusIntent(6)` -- the 6 is the number of status cards the player is about to receive and is rendered in the intent. The sim's Intent (monsters/base.py:36-59) collapses a C# AbstractIntent[] into one MoveType plus an `also` tuple with no status-count field, so the_insatiable.py:36 records `Intent(MoveType.BUFF, also=(MoveType.STATUS_CARD,))` and the 6 is lost. Same mechanism as aeonglass's StatusIntent(WitherAmount) and the empty intent array on the three BattleFriends; monster_state_machine's scope boundary item 2 records the whole AbstractIntent -> Intent mapping as audited by no seam. NOT LIVE: nothing in the sim consumes an intent's status count because the field does not exist, so no ported consumer can observe the loss today. Named trigger: adding a status-count field to Intent, or any observation/replay consumer that reads one.

ONE MECHANISM ACROSS THIS BATCH (rule 3), recorded at every site: the sim's monster ports drop PowerCmd.Apply's `applier` argument. C# is `Apply<T>(choiceContext, target, amount, applier, cardSource)` (PowerCmd.cs:67) and passes `base.Creature` at TheInsatiable.cs:125 (Sandpit) and :170 (StrengthPower), both applier=base.Creature; the sim's `PowerCmd.apply(hooks, target, power_cls, amount, applier=None)` (cmds.py:271-277) is called without it at the_insatiable.py:64 and :79. In C# a null applier additionally SKIPS the whole Hook.ModifyPowerAmountGiven pass (PowerCmd.cs:123-126) and changes the key FindExistingInstanceForStacking uses (PowerCmd.cs:78, :112). Same observable today, EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b06.py applier`): the sim has exactly six listener definitions that can see the argument -- powers.py:1172/1181 (ViciousPower, gated `name != "vulnerable" or applier is not self.owner`, powers.py:1167), powers.py:3101/3106 (_PossessPower, gated `applier is self.owner and name == self._stat_id and target.side == "player" and delta < 0`, powers.py:3092-3099), relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-38 (gated on `target is self.player`, never on applier) and relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53 (gated `applier is not self.player`, unsettling_lamp.py:47). None can distinguish `None` from the applying monster for a power this unit applies. Named trigger: porting any listener that reads `applier` positively (a monster-applier-sensitive relic), or porting PowerInstanceType so stacking is keyed by applier.
